name: Pygmy Swiftlet
rangeDescription: Philippines (except sulu archipelago)
description: A tiny, common swiftlet found over lowland forest. Gray below with a paler belly, a darker throat, and dark patches on the underside of the base of the forewing.

name: Glaucous Tanager
rangeDescription: Arid northeastern colombia and northern venezuela including isla margarita
description: Medium-sized tanager with gray head and back, blue-gray chest, white belly, and aquamarine wings. Often seen singly or in pairs; usually less abundant than similar Blue-gray Tanager.

name: Yellow-billed Giant-Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Fiji (taveuni and vanua levu)
description: A very large, robust honeyeater. Entirely drab grayish-olive, with yellowish wings and tail and a bright yellow bill and eye-ring.

name: Black-breasted Myzomela
rangeDescription: Timor (eastern lesser sundas)
description: A distinctive small black, white, and red honeyeater with a downcurved bill. Jet black with diagnostic red patches on rear crown, throat, and rump, as well as a clean white belly.

name: Laurel Pigeon
rangeDescription: Western canary islands (la palma, la gomera, and tenerife)
description: A Canary Island endemic found on rocky mountain slopes around the tree heath and laurel forest zone. Looks very dark, especially at a distance, with dark grey-purple wings, deep maroon underparts, and a tail with prominent pale tip unlike the co-occurring Bolle’s Pigeon.

name: Ruddy Crake
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern mexico to northwestern costa rica (northern guanacaste)
description: A small, elusive bird of freshwater marshes, damp fields, and roadside ditches; heard much more often than seen. Walks quietly and runs quickly, like all rails.

name: Bachman's Warbler
rangeDescription: Formerly southeastern usa; wintered to cuba and bahamas (probably extinct)
description: Jewel of a warbler, probably extinct. Male is distinctive, with a black patch on the lower throat and chest.

name: Prairie Falcon
rangeDescription: Arid north america (british columbia to northern mexico)
description: Large, brown-and-white falcon of dry, open areas in western North America. Pale brown above and white below, with dark streaks and prominent mustache.

name: Long-tailed Silky-flycatcher
rangeDescription: Mountains of costa rica and western panama (volcán de chiriquí)
description: Striking bird unlikely to be confused with any other species. Very long tail and obvious crest stand out, in addition to soft blue-gray body with yellow-green head and flanks.

name: Taiwan Hwamei
rangeDescription: Taiwan
description: Lightly streaked brown songbird with starkly pale eyes found in edge habitat and scrubby areas in Taiwan. Chinese Hwamei, which has been introduced in Taiwan, has an unstreaked head, dark eyes, and distinctive bluish lines behind the eyes.

name: Spot-tailed Goshawk
rangeDescription: Sulawesi region, including talisei (to northeast), muna and buton (to southeast)
description: A small pale hawk restricted to Sulawesi and nearby islands. Adult has a pale gray head, a bright yellow mark between bill and eye, and conspicuous white tail spots.

name: Annam Prinia
rangeDescription: Vietnam (langbian plateau)
description: A dull and poorly marked prinia with a strong bill and a long, graduated tail. Light brown above with faint dark streaking.

name: Gray-crested Helmetshrike
rangeDescription: Dry thornscrub of southwestern kenya and western tanzania
description: A sociable, cartoon-like black-and-white helmetshrike with a tall and fluffy gray crest, piercing yellow eyes, and small black patches on the sides of the breast. The black-and-white contrast is most apparent in flight, with white patches in the outer wing and at the end of the tail.

name: White-masked Antbird
rangeDescription: Northeastern peru (lower río pastaza and lower río morona)
description: Handsome antbird known only from a small area in northeastern Peru. Restricted to lowland rainforest in areas where the soil is sandy.

name: Junin Antpitta
rangeDescription: East slope of the andes of central peru (junín, south of the río perené and río paucartambo, north of the río mantaro, and west of the río ene)
description: Medium-sized, plain antpitta found in a limited area of the eastern Andes in south central Peru. It is uniform brown lacking strong field marks, but the pale eyering helps separate it from the similar Oxapampa Antpitta.

name: Sjöstedt's Owlet
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southwestern cameroon to gabon, northern congo, and northwestern democratic republic of the congo
description: A small owlet of lowland and foothill forest interior with intricate barring patterns over most of its body, including the buff-and-black underparts, the gray-and-white head, the rufous back, and the black-and-white wings and tail. Primarily nocturnal, but sometimes calls around first light.

name: Long-bearded Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Alpine grassland of east-central new guinea
description: A long, slender honeyeater of subalpine forest and shrubland in eastern New Guinea. All sooty gray-black plumage with long tail and very long, thin, curved bill, long white, whispy beard from the base of the bill, and a yellow-orange wattle at the back of the eye.

name: Eye-ringed Parrotbill
rangeDescription: Southern china (southern sichuan and northern yunnan)
description: Gregarious long-tailed little bird. Restricted to southwestern China and adjacent northern Myanmar, where it inhabits grassy and scrubby areas, as well as bamboo stands and secondary growth, in mountains and foothills.

name: Bonaparte's Nightjar
rangeDescription: Lowlands of sumatra, belitung (off southeastern sumatra), and borneo
description: Small dark-brown nightjar of lowland forests. Bright white bib often noticeable.

name: Red-billed Woodcreeper
rangeDescription: Southeastern venezuela to the guianas and brazil north of the amazon river
description: Large, stout-billed woodcreeper of tall rainforest in northeastern Amazonia. Plumage entirely rufous-brown with no barring or streaking; note thick reddish bill, white throat, and prominent white whisker mark (bill of young birds is dark brown).
